qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

While I welcome the Commission’s desire to promote educational and scientific collaboration at regional level, I note that the new plan introduces costly bodies such as the Science Diplomacy Centre and the Mediterranean University. This increase in the number of external institutions comes at a time when the Member States are being asked to make major budgetary sacrifices, and local communities in less developed regions lack basic infrastructure. I therefore ask the Commission: 1.
What is the expected total administrative and operational cost of setting up and running these new regional centres, platforms and campaigns?

On the basis of which efficiency criteria does the Commission justify allocating nonrepayable funds to parallel bodies such as these outside Europe’s borders when public services in disadvantaged European regions are underfunded?
What measurable performance indicators will the Commission use to show that this spending is bringing direct and tangible benefits for EU citizens?
